scenario.label: Injected test data
scenario.reference: GNSS drag-off spoofing: Humphreys et al., ION GNSS 2008; the need for independent multilateration or receiver cross-checks: Strohmeier et al., IEEE Commun. Surveys & Tutorials 2015.
scenario.simulates: A real, recorded aircraft's reported position is dragged away by 0.1 NM per poll up to 20 NM. Each step is small enough to stay inside the kinematic limits, so no detection fires: a slow drag-off by a consistent spoofer is a known blind spot of single-receiver plausibility checks.
scenario.title: Gradual drift (documented gap)

scenario.label: Injected test data
scenario.reference: Message modification (attack background: Schäfer et al., ACNS 2013). GNSS spoofing of position sources: Humphreys et al., ION GNSS 2008.
scenario.simulates: A real, recorded aircraft's reported position steps 20 NM sideways in a single report and stays shifted, as if its messages had been modified in transit. This is a step, not a gradual drag-off: it is caught at the instant of the jump (see the gradual_drift gap).
scenario.title: Position step (20 NM)

events.explanation: Registration N12345 is a US N-number, whose Mode S address is a061d9, but the aircraft transmits adfc10 (a United States block).
events.title: ICAO address allocation mismatch

events.explanation: Address adfd59 is in the United States allocation (ICAO Annex 10 Table 9-1) but registration G-ZZZA carries the nationality mark of United Kingdom.
